verdict.reasoning: Patient states he woke up about an hour ago and then could not move his left arm: "I woke up this morning, about an hour ago, and I couldn't move my left arm any more."
He describes painless loss of movement: "I feel no pain but just, uh, can't move it."
He reports tingling on the left side of the face since onset: "I feel a bit of tingling on the left side of my face" and "since I woke up... so an hour ago."

He describes difficulty drinking consistent with dysphagia: "I was trying to drink earlier and I'd be bold a bit" and doctor clarifies "you have some difficulties swallowing, is that right?" Patient answers, "Um, yeah."
He notes slower, more effortful speech: "it's more complicated maybe, maybe um, be more slow. I need to think more about it."
He denies leg involvement: when asked about left leg symptoms he answers, "No, but um, I feel a bit of tingling on the left side of my face."
When asked about facial asymmetry, he denies noticing it: "Have you noticed any kind of, um, asymmetry in your face... anything different at all?" Patient: "Mmm, no, not really."

Doctor asks about discoloration and temperature; patient denies both: "is there any discoloration in your hand?" Patient: "Um, no." and "does your hand feel cold?" Patient: "Mmm, no, really the, mmm, the arm feels fine, apart from me not being able to move it."
Patient states: "I have, uh, type two diabetes".
Patient states: "and, uh, high blood pressure." which is hypertension.
In response to medication question: "I'm taking Metformin losartan and Amlodipine."
Same line: "I'm taking Metformin losartan and Amlodipine."
Same line: "I'm taking Metformin losartan and Amlodipine."
On allergies: "Um, only penicillin, I believe."
Family history: "my dad has got, um, heart disease."
Living situation: Doctor asks "are you normally living alone?" Patient: "Uh, yes."
Smoking history: Doctor asks "Do you smoke at all?" Patient: "Uh, I used to." indicating ex-smoker.
Alcohol: Patient says "I will have a few drinks over the weekend. Um, maybe a, a couple more during the week." and specifies "beers, uh, like pints."

Doctor explicitly suspects stroke and the listed symptoms are present: left arm paralysis, facial tingling, swallowing difficulty, and slowed speech. Doctor: "I'm concerned that some of the symptoms you've got may be, um, symptoms of a stroke."
Hypertension is documented in history: "I have, uh, type two diabetes and, uh, high blood pressure." as part of assessment.
Type 2 diabetes is documented: "I have, uh, type two diabetes" and is part of the assessment context.

Doctor arranges emergency ambulance for suspected stroke: "I'm gonna arrange one of my colleagues next to me to, um, call an ambulance to your home address now" and links symptoms to "symptoms of a stroke." (999 is simply UK emergency number).

Doctor instructs: "maybe you could, uh, leave the front door, um, unlocked, sit in the hallway." and later "make sure the the front door's open. Sit in the hallway, by the front door so that they've got access".
Doctor states intention to remain on the line: "what I'm gonna do is, I'm gonna stay on the line until they reach there. Just to make sure that you're OK."

Doctor anticipates A&E assessment and acute stroke therapy: "they'll probably take you down to, um, the local hospital, A and E. And then, they'll they will ring through for the, um, the stroke doctor to assess you, to see whether they can give you any kind of, um, treatment for that."
There is no discussion about changing or not changing hypertension or diabetes management; these topics are only elicited in history, with no explicit plan stated about them.
